title: The Flirtatious Villainess
paragraphs: “My lords, the heroes… I can’t help but be concerned about the Filolials swimming behind the ship…”
Éclair interrupts the conversation over something trivial. I turn my gaze toward the Filolial-samas I’ve raised.
“I wish I could have raised more of them.”
“You still want more even with this many…?”
“In some of our previous runs, I’ve raised even more than this.”

This time, aside from Father’s restrictions, I simply couldn’t secure enough of them. It’s all because that breeder’s ranch ended up in such a state. Since I only bought a few from the Monster Merchant and managed to procure a few more on my own, I’m far from satisfied. Ah… Back then, I made countless attempts searching for Filo-tan. But Filo-tan turned out to be Sakura-chan… It’s so frustrating.
“If this is all we got even with Eclair-san holding back, then… let’s just put up with it.”
“……I get it. If things had gone differently, the situation would’ve been even worse.”
“It’s so chaotic it’s exhausting. Elmelo, you must be tired from teaching both the Filolials and everyone else all sorts of things, right?”
“No…… Everyone just sang and acted out stories at the venue, so it wasn’t that bad……”

Zou really is a great Zou, isn’t he? He doesn’t seem tired at all. Thanks to the guidance of senior Filolial-samas like Yuki-chan and Kou, the Idol activities on the island were a success. And it was Zou who contributed to that. He really is a capable Zou. I’ll definitely keep that in mind.
“…I don’t know how to put it, but I’ve been so caught up in everything that I haven’t had a moment to think about Ren… I have to find him soon.”
“Searching for the missing Sword Hero, huh… Being a hero sure is a busy job, isn’t it?”
And so, even though they were supposedly on vacation, Father and the others returned from Cal Mira Island looking quite exhausted.
Right after returning from Cal Mira Island, we ended up meeting up with our rivals in Melromarc. Apparently, our rivals had been conducting diplomatic negotiations there alongside the queens.
“Heroes of the Shield and Spear, how was your training on Cal Mira Island?”
The representative of the Shusaku clan asked us this upon our return.
“I’ve heard you spent very fruitful days on the island.”
It seems the queen is also curious about our elegant days on the island.
“I heard you were partying hard on the island. You’re still the same old Spear Hero, aren’t you?”
Our Rival says this with a look of exasperation, cradling his Assistant on his lap. “A wild party,” is what he calls it. We simply succeeded in our Idol careers with elegance and panache.
“I can’t deny it… Honestly, those were days with no time to rest…”

Éclair says this with a sigh. What’s that supposed to mean? Is she complaining? This is exactly why stubborn knights who only have training on their minds are no good. I wish they’d have a little more leeway to enjoy the situation, like pandas and elephants do.
“How rude. While you were conducting your foolish diplomacy, Filolial-sama occupied Cal Mira Island. Rival, that’s not a place where you’ll gain support, so give it up.”
“Isn’t that wrong in all sorts of ways, though?”
“I think so, too.”
The panda and the elephant are pointing something out.
“To begin with, it shouldn’t be called a wild party—it should be called a live performance.”
“Well, that’s not quite right, but… never mind. It’s too much of a hassle.”
“Ahaha… That’s just like you, Motoyasu-kun.”
Father agreed with a dry laugh. He’s the only one who really gets me.
“So… I assume you’ve already been briefed, but I couldn’t find Ren.”
“I’ve heard… Seriously, where did he go? It’s such a hassle.”
“That’s true… It seems the Spear Hero fully understands the Sword Hero’s personality. If he still can’t be found despite that, we should probably expand the search area even further.”
“Yeah, I think so too. You know… there are all sorts of troublemakers on the loose right now.”

“I know. Well, since Gaelion remembers the enemies from the looped memories to some extent, we’ve already managed to contain them pretty well. I think things will work out more or less once we deal with those guys.”
“Yeah. Thanks as always, Gaelion-chan.”
“I am… I’m so happy to be praised by Naofumi!”
Father is smiling back at Rival. He’s just responding out of courtesy! Don’t get the wrong idea!
The Assistant is watching this in silence. It’s been a while since then—has anything changed?
“So, Gaelion-chan, you went on a diplomatic mission while we were on Cal Mira Island, right? How did it go?”
“Yes. We also participated in the diplomatic talks and reported the warning signs of the Spirit Tortoise’s revival.”
It seems the representative of the Shusaku clan and the queen are both here to report to us.
“To put it simply, they didn’t budge an inch on our proposal… They just kept insisting, ‘If a crisis is looming, bring the Four Holy Heroes here’…”
“That villainess from their country just gave a smile that seemed slightly displeased with our proposal, haha.”
It seems the diplomatic talks didn’t go very well. Right here, Rival raises and lowers his hand as if to tell the Shusaku Clan and the Queen to hold back.
“For someone called a ‘wicked woman,’ you can tell she’s having a hard time. Her approval rating back home is high.”
“Who are you talking about?”
That’s right. It seems there’s a person here I don’t quite understand either.

“Hmm… She’s a woman who, when she tried to further corrupt an already rotten royal court—only to find it was already too corrupt to do anything—is now working hard to elevate herself just so she can be brought down by a hero.”
“Um… How is that any different from the First Princess of Melromarc?”
“It’s embarrassing that my own daughter is being compared to her.”
The queen answers Father’s question with a sigh.
“That one is a thoroughly evil woman, while this one is a good person with just a hint of wickedness. She might be similar in essence to the Queen of Melromarc, though.”
“Huh…”
Father doesn’t seem to get it either.

“So it sounds like diplomacy isn’t going to go well until we get there… or maybe, given the timeline, we won’t be able to stop the Spirit Tortoise’s revival? In that case, we should go to minimize the damage as much as possible, right?”

We’re all set. After all, that’s why we’ve been training all this time. We’re strong enough now that we could easily defeat the Spirit Tortoise. Come to think of it… the cave leading into the Spirit Tortoise’s body is pretty narrow, so I’m worried Zou might not be able to fit through.
“Ah, there’s no need to worry about that.”
At this point, our Rival states this with surprising confidence.
“I’ve been wondering why the seal keeps breaking even though the heroes haven’t done anything during our previous runs, so Gaelion went to that country to keep watch.”
“Yeah. So?”

“Well, Gaelion was keeping watch just in case, and sure enough—or rather, as expected—I figured out the cause and took care of it. So unless Naofumi and the others show up, there’s practically no chance the Spirit Tortoise will be revived.”
“Huh? Wait, why?”

“Well, I thought there was no way, but sure enough, it showed up—I was flabbergasted. This is all thanks to the knowledge I gathered in the first world—now that I’ve nipped one troublesome problem in the bud, I’m sure there won’t be any issues.”
That’s the kind of nonsense our Rival was spouting. She’s the only one who seems to understand what’s going on, while we’re just left scratching our heads. Explain it properly, will you!
“Um… so, does that mean Gaelion-chan resolved something regarding the Spirit Tortoise beforehand?”

“You can think of it that way. Spear Hero, if we end up in a loop where Gaelion isn’t there, make sure to let the Spirit Tortoise know. That way, it’ll stay asleep, and the seal won’t be broken until the scheduled time. Well… since the wave will be over by the scheduled time, the Spirit Tortoise will just keep sleeping.”

After saying that, Rival set the date and time, and told us to just send the Brionac deep into the cave leading into the Spirit Tortoise’s body from the entrance. I have absolutely no idea what’s going on.
“Well… since Gaelion-chan is the Dragon Emperor and apparently once possessed the memories of the Dragon King, I guess we can assume it’ll be fine?”
“That’s right!”
“Is there absolutely no chance that Ren could break the seal?”

“That’s because Gaelion got there ahead of time and set up a powerful barrier around the seal. Not even the Sword Hero—still just a weakling—let alone Takt’s crew, could break it. And if anyone tries to mess with it, Gaelion will get a notification, so we’ll know.”
Rival is glaring at us with an incredibly infuriating attitude. Who’s going to praise you, I wonder? No one’s going to praise you!
“Even if the Sword Hero does show up, he’ll be like a moth flying into a flame.”
“It’d be great if Ren got caught right there, though.”
Father is really hoping Rival’s trap works out.
“He’s more capable in so many ways than that Spear Hero from somewhere.”
Panda! What’s that supposed to mean?! Are you trying to say our Rival is better than me!?
“So, even though the diplomacy failed, I didn’t go down without a fight and managed to solve the problem.”
“Ah, thanks, Gaelion-chan. You’re a lifesaver.”
“Of course! It’s only natural!”
Guh… Rival… Now that it’s come to this, I’ll have to find Ren myself and hand him over to Father.
“As for the rest, if we set up a strong barrier at the triggers that unlock the Four Spirits’ seals in various locations, we’ll be able to subdue any Sword Heroes who come seeking power.”
“Yeah. Can you handle that? I’d like to avoid any major casualties caused by something Ren might do.”
“Leave it to me!”
“Thank you, Gaelion-chan.”

Father approaches Rival to thank him. Rival, seizing the moment, leans forward with a look that says, “Pet me, please.” Father glances at his Assistant with a troubled expression, wondering if it’s okay to pet him, but the Assistant, looking bored, quietly closes his eyes and ignores him. Tell him no! Why on earth did you come along with Rival in the first place? My curse fails to reach him, and Father ends up petting Rival’s head.
“I-I… thank you!”
Rival, having been petted, looks delighted—anyone can see that. His tail is wagging like crazy! I’m starting to feel murderous.
“Boo…”
Sakura-chan is voicing her protest here. You need to speak up more!
“Boo! I say!”
“Boo…”
“Come on, come on, just put up with this much. Gaelion didn’t come to the island, after all. Sakura and the others have played with us plenty already… right?”
“Boo…”
Sakura’s protest is getting quieter.
“You don’t have to make concessions to Rival!”
“I wonder if it’s really fair to say she’s less understanding than Filolial, though.”
Panda, you’re saying one too many things!
“Kou-san, you shouldn’t copy him.”
“Eh… I kind of feel like it’d be okay if we were dealing with a dragon, though?”
“This is where we need to make a concession. Otherwise, we’ll just end up causing more trouble. Yuki-san, you understand that, right?”
For some reason, Zou is lecturing Kou and Yuki-chan here.
“I’m extremely reluctant…”
Oh, it seems Yuki-chan understands my point of view!
“Motoyasu-sama, I suggest you exercise patience here. Let’s show the composure of the strong. We’ve already had success on Cal Mira Island!”
“Quite right!”

Father must hold this success in high regard! There was no need to worry about Rival’s hocus-pocus—those events where it wasn’t even clear if they’d succeed! I suppose protesting just because I gave Rival a little pat on the back would only cause Father trouble.
“I have various points I’d like to raise, but I’ve learned that it’s ultimately better to just go with the flow in situations like this.”
“It seems our serious lady knight has developed a sense of detachment…”
“I think that’s for the best, too.”
And so, Panda and Zou are nodding in mysterious agreement to Éclair, who is guarding Father.
“Ahaha… Anyway, thank you, everyone. Let’s keep our guard up and do our best to find Ren.”
“Exactly! After that, we just need to gather the remaining Seven Star Heroes hiding in various places!”
And so, in this manner, we decided on our next steps with Rival and the nation’s leaders. Then… this happened after the meeting ended.
“…Gaelion.”
“What is it? Big Sis, what’s up?”
The Assistant, who had been sitting silently on Rival’s lap and watching the proceedings, spoke up while we were taking a break after the meeting ended.
“I think I’ll head home now.”
“Really? Are you done already? You could stay a little longer.”
Then the Assistant looked at Rival and shook her head.
“I’ve seen how hard you’ve been working on all sorts of things. And I get that it’s been tough for you, too.”
“You understand, then?”
Had the Assistant really been with Rival for that long? Well, I’m sure there’s no need to worry about it.
“…I realize I can’t let myself fall behind either. It’s no good just standing here watching.”
